tuduc.column: Brick columns of the Stele Pavilion
tuduc.column_des: The roof of the Stele Pavilion rests on four large, round brick columns. The brick structure keeps the building stable enough to shelter the stone stele, which weighs about 22 tonnes and stands in the middle of the pavilion.
tuduc.architectureDetail_des: This second preview point verifies that only the detail closest to the center of the camera receives the interaction.
tuduc.vanbia_des: The bell-shaped pediment of the stele features a raised dragon-and-cloud motif. A dragon’s face appears at the top, with its curling tail below, surrounded by clouds and flame-like details.
tuduc.thanvanbia_des: Inscribed with 4,935 Chinese characters across both sides, the Khiêm Cung Ký stele bears the longest stone inscription in Vietnam. It is also the only surviving royal artifact that fully preserves Emperor Tự Đức’s own handwritten text. A remarkable work of artistry and stone carving, the inscription offers a personal glimpse into the emperor’s concerns for his changing country. It also describes the landscape around his tomb, where hills bearing the name “Khiêm” seem to gather in tribute. For visitors, the stele is both a historical record and a moving connection to the spirit of Huế.
tuduc.steleBase_des: The base is shaped with curved “quỳ” legs and measures 100 cm high, 309 cm wide and 162.5 cm deep. Its outer faces are carved in relief and openwork with dragons, clouds, a tiger-face motif (hổ phù) and folded S-shaped meanders.

stele.title: The Khiêm Cung Ký Stele
stele.summary: The stele is a single block of granite from Thanh Hóa (known as Thanh stone). It is 407 cm high, 259 cm wide, 48 cm at its thickest and weighs an estimated 22 tonnes. Emperor Tự Đức wrote the text himself: the front carries 2,319 characters in regular script and the back 2,537 characters in running script. The stele is recognised as a national treasure.

steleHeading.title: The dragon-and-cloud heading
steleHeading.summary: The heading is 97 cm high and 287.5 cm wide. It is shaped like a stone chime and carved in relief with a “long vân” (dragon and cloud) motif. In court art, the dragon is the image associated with the emperor.

steleBase.title: The quỳ-leg base and stone platform
steleBase.summary: The base is 100 cm high, 309 cm wide and 162.5 cm deep, shaped with curved “quỳ” legs and finely carved: its outer faces show dragons, clouds, a tiger-face motif (hổ phù) and folded S-shaped meanders in relief and openwork. The stele and its base stand on a two-tier platform of Thanh stone with steps on all four sides.

tuDuc.name: Tomb of Tu Duc
tuDuc.description: The tomb of Emperor Tự Đức (Khiêm Lăng) in Huế. The scene recreates the Stele Pavilion and the Khiêm Cung Ký stele the emperor wrote himself.

aboutPage.label: About
aboutPage.p1: Vietnam Virtual is a website for visiting Vietnamese heritage sites in 3D. Open the map, pick a place and walk around it right in your browser, with nothing to install.
aboutPage.p2: Right now you can visit the Tomb of Tự Đức in Huế and a gallery of antiquities. Every artifact has a 3D model you can turn, zoom and read notes on.
aboutPage.p3: It is a graduation project built with photos and 3D models from many authors. Their credits are listed below.
